content_voiceover: This is a continuation of the same table, now covering entities with decreased platelet counts and various clinical syndromes. Gray platelet syndrome shows large pale platelets with absent alpha granules, heterogeneous response to agonists, and is associated with myelofibrosis and pulmonary fibrosis, caused by NBEAL2, inherited as autosomal recessive or dominant. Wiskott Aldrich syndrome, highlighted here, has decreased count with small platelets and delta granule deficiency, impaired aggregation, and the classic clinical triad of eczema, infections, and immunodeficiency plus autoimmune disease and malignancy risk, it is X linked and caused by the WAS gene, this is extremely high yield. Then we move into the bone marrow failure group, all with normal platelet size and normal function but decreased count. Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia involves MPL and leads to bone marrow failure. Thrombocytopenia absent radii features decreased megakaryocytes with limb abnormalities. Amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia with radio ulnar synostosis involves HOXA11 with skeletal abnormalities and hearing loss. Familial platelet disorder with predisposition to AML involves RUNX1. Paris Trousseau Jacobsen syndrome features large platelets with large granules, pancytopenia, and facial and cardiac anomalies, involving ETS1 and FLT1. And GATA1 mutation causes X linked thrombocytopenia with thalassemia and anemia.
keypoints: Gray platelet syndrome: large pale platelets missing alpha granules, NBEAL2 gene
Wiskott Aldrich syndrome: small platelets, eczema, infections, immunodeficiency, X linked
CAMT and TAR both present with decreased count and normal platelet size
FPD AML involves RUNX1 and predisposes to myelodysplasia and leukemia
Paris Trousseau syndrome features large platelets with large granules plus facial and cardiac anomalies
keypoint_voiceover: Focus on Wiskott Aldrich syndrome as the highest yield entity on this slide, small platelets, X linked, and the eczema infection immunodeficiency triad. Then remember gray platelet syndrome for absent alpha granules, and RUNX1 mutation for familial platelet disorder with AML predisposition, a classic germline leukemia predisposition syndrome.
